I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, **Lincoln Media Foundation** was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. _That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation._ They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the _first place._ I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and **[every dollar you give to LMF goes directly toward keeping reporters like me in the field](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=a9c35df5c86e4fe7a6d6cb591d891e94&_e=zxfY8wbRAERvf2BExxxuMYPZ9o2xwBlLw-99SLTZixjMW8zylRGhfOLpfvWWgSpvYbf_TMAK6XmHkYCGYvPtbvtjOLIBTz0mYMc4JTtdmhKeG6iXfJqlfU3t4rCUy3nqGbqV7Aww8IkqMwl5HJWGa5YYh8Hjy0Jsg8MNt2HNlq4ATNXDqY3sKIB5Gb6PKjsCT-VJX3Ll9lMCzr_WFEqUKowo7zjm9NIyaupr2mfwBTqixKK6pvOevb34ZvMYCsG4etzlulPcVG6LrBWO2OPnKGjswLymReQN4eR1LZ6-jt2ElWcEkTPqBIt0Yz3oAcnEsavogrbbF3LynyypyIOqJhRjw6qbteErHECH7NDg8phipLQMYfl-4pG7vMZgYr7QiumOP42aAd8PyeJxm8XTOmooo5rqCxMKU_WXsUBU47FDIMNpLWAFyJwEDFKTJpo2Z-BIyEAdv_L4djMSa5N4ibOAjPYCan1Rdv4DLO4K9KHoAJ50gDGX2Int14wGv7KWD2CDPq2zPSw6c8wrC9AxpI-gobo4I3G5j8Wf9Nsp47pV4joYjyPRybbdrQlqydWeEWfZKZ-3UMZ-qsj2QYmIWqeG0Sh0ou2UwY09ZxcWnsrHFlm-sxhg75q2RF1yLm3LNj-VPsfPW-XTLkJdcofVDeLPArmkelaPtk4a7pPNbnB7CwilLC-iUAGZXUHZaG_tkE-eGNPg69RgCLj2NYVyzf4dFg-eSGM-j7z5s3t57Go%3D)** - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them.

clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Friend, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. A few years ago, if you said an avowed socialist could be leading the Senate race in Texas, I'd have called you crazy. It's happening. James Talarico — the 36-year-old "minister" challenging conservative Ken Paxton — is currently leading by six points. Not in Massachusetts. Not in Vermont. _**In Texas**_. Talarico hasn't called himself a socialist radical. He doesn't have to. His own words do the work for him. He's said: ❌ Capitalism is an "oppressive system" and must be dismantled❌ The American flag is a "complicated" symbol
❌ White men are the greatest domestic terrorist threat in this country❌ God is "non-binary"
❌ The Bible is pro-abortion
❌ Christianity is "the most violent religion"
❌ There are six genders, not two That's not a caricature. That's the man in his own words. Strip away the "Christian" branding, and the policy agenda underneath is standard-issue far left: open borders, government-run healthcare, abortion up to birth, gun control, welfare for illegal immigrants, and a war on parental rights in schools.
And Texas isn't the only place this is happening. In Florida, DSA candidate Angie Nixon just won her primary by 12 points. In Oklahoma, DSA candidate N'Kiyla "Jasmine" Thomas won hers by 22. If either candidate wins in November, they'd be the first Democratic socialists ever elected to the U.S. Senate. And let's be honest. Socialist is their label meant to soften what they truly are **—** Marxists. **This rise of full-blown Communism isn't a fringe problem in blue states. | | | I introduced a bipartisan bill this week, and the reaction from Trump's own FBI Director tells you everything you need to know about why it's necessary. **The bill is called the No FLOCK Act** , and I introduced it with a Republican colleague, because this shouldn't be a partisan issue. It targets Flock Safety and other automated license plate reader networks that have quietly turned into a nationwide surveillance system. Here's what's actually happening on the ground. A Washington Post investigation found at least 69 police officials who have been accused, charged, or convicted of abusing this technology — using it to track wives, girlfriends, ex-partners, and people they had no legitimate reason to be watching. In Kentucky, one officer used the system more than 2,000 times to stalk his ex-girlfriend. **_And this week, when senators pushed FBI Director Kash Patel on it directly, he didn't express any concern. He defended the technology outright._** Let me be clear about what our bill actually does. It doesn't ban this technology outright, and it doesn't stop legitimate public safety uses like finding stolen cars or locating missing children. What it does is put teeth behind real limits: if a state doesn't restrict license plate readers to a defined set of legitimate uses, it loses some of its federal highway funding. No more unchecked expansion. No more excuses. Because right now, there is functionally no limit on what this data can be used for once it's collected, or who can access it. body:
Shapiro wants government officials to enter your home without a warrant. Tell him no.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/l43mm3yfKOF?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | |
Peter,
I took an oath to defend the Constitution of the United States. I took it when I put on the uniform. I take it seriously.So when I read that Josh Shapiro’s Department of Health is proposing regulations that would allow government officials to enter your home without a warrant, I didn’t just disagree with it. I was appalled.**The Fourth Amendment is not optional. It is not negotiable. And it does not have a public health exception.** Shapiro’s proposed regulations — buried inside more than 500 pages of bureaucratic language — would give his Department of Health the power to enter private residences and businesses to investigate disease outbreaks. No warrant. No judicial oversight. Just a government official at your door.This is the same administration that wants to access your confidential medical records without consent, interview your children at school without telling you, and reimpose mask mandates by regulation.And all of it bypasses the legislature — because Shapiro knows elected representatives would never vote for this.In 2021, Pennsylvanians amended their own constitution to limit the Governor’s power to do exactly this. The voters were clear. Shapiro is ignoring them.**The public comment period closes September 21. Tell the state that the Fourth Amendment still applies in Pennsylvania:**
---
| [SUBMIT YOUR PUBLIC COMMENT](mailto:RA-DHCHAPTR27PROPREG@pa.gov?subject=Rulemaking%20%2310-242%3A%20Communicable%20and%20Noncommunicable%20Diseases%3B%20IRRC%20%233490&body=)
---

Tell them these regulations should be withdrawn and that policy this consequential belongs in the legislature, not in a 500-page regulatory filing.**Pennsylvanians said never again in 2021. Let’s make sure he hears it.**
– Stacy

If you're on social media this week, you've probably seen it: the all-caps story about the Tennessee high school principal, the football game, and the prayer. "HAPPENED AT A TENNESSEE FOOTBALL GAME -- NOT A JOKE. CHRISTIANITY IS NOW THE TARGET OF PERSECUTION."
It's true. And it's also twenty-six years old.
Both things matter, so let's get them both right -- because the truth is stronger than the viral version, and this week it picked up a coda nobody saw coming.

# Hull Campaign Responds to Deb Haaland Press Conference
---
| | | | | | **RIO RANCHO, New Mexico (September 17, 2026) –** Gregg Hull, Republican nominee for New Mexico Governor, issued the following statement in response to Democratic nominee Deb Haaland’s press conference today calling for a moratorium on new data centers in New Mexico.
“My opponent’s call for a moratorium on data centers is suspicious considering it comes two days after it was discovered that she took nearly $100,000 from Oracle and Project Jupiter executives,” Hull said. “She was caught with her hand in the cookie jar and this press conference was just an attempt to do damage control.”
[Campaign finance reports from the last reporting period show Haaland received multiple donations totaling $87,200 from Oracle America](https://us.list-manage.com/mlv3nSA2l6n?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810) and executives with Clayco, the company constructing Project Jupiter. Oracle donated $12,400 to Haaland, while another $74,800 came from employees including top leadership at both Oracle and Clayco. Several of those donations were max-out donations of $12,400.
Gregg Hull has not accepted nor solicited donations from big data.

**Part 1: What Happened in February 2025**
On February 11, 2025, DHS announced it was terminating four FEMA employees -- Chief Financial Officer Mary Comans, two program analysts, and a grant specialist -- for "circumventing leadership to unilaterally make egregious payments for luxury NYC hotels for migrants."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee5add83-aaa1-4cfb-80dc-6211e93681af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The trigger was Elon Musk, whose Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) said it had uncovered roughly $59 million in FEMA payments to New York City to reimburse migrant hotel costs -- with the White House stating about $19 million of that covered hotel rooms directly. At the time, New York City was housing thousands of migrants, including at the Roosevelt Hotel in Midtown Manhattan, under its "right to shelter" obligations. Acting FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton subsequently suspended further payments...

# Hull Campaign Responds to Deb Haaland Press Conference
---
| | | | | | **RIO RANCHO, New Mexico (September 17, 2026) –** Gregg Hull, Republican nominee for New Mexico Governor, issued the following statement in response to Democratic nominee Deb Haaland’s press conference today calling for a moratorium on new data centers in New Mexico.
“My opponent’s call for a moratorium on data centers is suspicious considering it comes two days after it was discovered that she took nearly $100,000 from Oracle and Project Jupiter executives,” Hull said. “She was caught with her hand in the cookie jar and this press conference was just an attempt to do damage control.”
[Campaign finance reports from the last reporting period show Haaland received multiple donations totaling $87,200 from Oracle America](https://us.list-manage.com/DBOrP6fEGEM?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810) and executives with Clayco, the company constructing Project Jupiter. Oracle donated $12,400 to Haaland, while another $74,800 came from employees including top leadership at both Oracle and Clayco. Several of those donations were max-out donations of $12,400.
Gregg Hull has not accepted nor solicited donations from big data.

****
#### **Forward Party CEO, Lindsey Williams Drath, Vows Pursuit of Equity****in Ballot Access After US Supreme Court Petition Denial**
**_Washington D.C. – September 17, 2026_** _–_ “Today we learned the United States Supreme Court’s Tenth Circuit has chosen to deny New Mexico Forward Party’s petition for injunctive relief in its lawsuit, ‘New Mexico Forward Party v. Toulouse Oliver’, preventing two Forwardists, Bob Perls and Michael Vigil, from being added to the November 3rd ballot. “Though we are disappointed in the court’s decision to not add Perls and Vigil to the ballot in time for the immediate upcoming election, we remain encouraged and steadfast in our belief that unconstitutional signature requirements in the state of New Mexico will soon fall when the case is heard in full. “Onerous and opaque signature requirements are just one of the many ways the legacy parties lock out potential competition at the polls, reducing candidate options for voters. There are examples of questionable ballot access requirements in other states across the country wherein independent candidates are met with mountainous tasks and red tape to be listed on the ballot, while Democrats and Republicans step over relative molehills. “This moment further underscores the need for the Federal Election Commission to recognize Forward as a national party committee in 2028. Without it, the independent movement is severely disadvantaged, preventing full coordination across every surface of the political process. I look forward to the proceedings of the New Mexico Forward Party’s lawsuit at a later date and thank them for their continued diligence in pursuing this matter.” — _Forward Party CEO, Lindsey Williams Drath_ **About Forward Party** The Forward Party is bringing moderates, conservatives, and progressives together to heal our political divisions, find our shared ground, and create a brighter future for America. Forward Party candidates are accountable to the voters, and they will focus on solutions, not partisan fighting, in order to serve their constituents better.

subject: The Constitution already settled this
body:
A new census proposal would stop counting millions of our neighbors. Citizenship is the answer. | | | Peter, today is Citizenship Day, and this year it comes with a warning. A new federal proposal would stop counting immigrants without green cards in the 2030 census. **That count decides how many House seats each state gets and how federal funding is distributed. 1** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIGjw8YzSH_UAUmMq7WLV0krCNSeQgLJ3AAolc0INa2dHYXohOJ_bhe4StWnNN7ErdZ2UglUm11t7DmS4pKCpB0Ljho9zsJM1pOZEtemGo5qG-Xio_Nqo0QvjmcvBcvXGzoeUChMY7EFWPd3qFTGmBFlMb6M66j6kfvZvvBk9ieIL_TRsem3oDYmB2YwzbWpDRvUM7f9Lq-6iqpbt814PN0k6z1fS_EzQcvcOy8Tq-Kw60VdcsNbEYOBrXSdpXq2n9uuMP9xaf70wmdYgcAAsLku4VnzqAUDvXYRE8Kf6u_TUrkmufBPKwxDxV_3WRTqDKyFGSTwiqZCi1OTwgWxa4T1UMLRGm_tcMlXQRgwOLYs/4u4/b7BSJ3HBSlyUzVGttorXjA/h0/h001.eeqfCkWeawMyo3s_rf2jxmP0ZAhkuu9ZAp6ltdeZxyw) _That means millions of people who live, work, and raise families here would not be counted._ They would be intentionally left out of the census, and the communities they live in could lose representation and federal funding.1 **[Every person in this country counts, and the fight for citizenship is as urgent as ever. Will you chip in $10 today to power the movement for citizenship?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIGjw8YzSH_UAUmMq7WLV0krCNSeQgLJ3AAolc0INa2dHYXohOJ_bhe4StWnNN7Ery6poj6WxygG7MM6yNGQC-EzZq4M-4SF1-Yl2v9-Ea_m7Gj9K8_nFGWMNiiEPb1oNcJYEWfQ7YXLuraveQjgzKSCyIP2kTwz0duQfEfz5HksV_7onJEfZvgOqtx9AeIZNLvaisz2fpJF2EvNB3AXASf_7J7BES6sbdDx85k2NKnVH_-76aEGiERJuncqR5TvHesAp7U5IlmRXcSngHih_QKSf47gOpHjnNCzqn2a7e9FkJNdHc2W6_-Xyc7FQYs9P-v6gWdGBXdAtLhOOJxK4wbJw4PA_BZQv4tfvZOdAg3bfZtijeL_69tOpswF0oLw6/4u4/b7BSJ3HBSlyUzVGttorXjA/h1/h001.R3NmezvE5mbnb4gYrKMG1mYWb3JcN42ZbjLzAOM7BYA)** The Constitution already answered this question. The census counts the "whole number of persons in each state." Just this June, the Supreme Court turned back an attempt to restrict birthright citizenship. This proposal recycles many of the same arguments.1 This is the thousand-cuts pattern again: another attempt to shrink the definition of who belongs here and leave millions of working people uncounted and unheard. So on this Citizenship Day, we keep pushing for a country that sees all of us. We want a country where our neighbors are counted, not erased. We want one where the people who keep this country running have a permanent home. **[Home is here, and no rule change alters that. A pathway to citizenship is the permanent protection our communities need, and Congress can deliver it. clean_body: A new census proposal would stop counting millions of our neighbors. Citizenship is the answer. | | | Peter, today is Citizenship Day, and this year it comes with a warning. A new federal proposal would stop counting immigrants without green cards in the 2030 census. That count decides how many House seats each state gets and how federal funding is distributed. 1 That means millions of people who live, work, and raise families here would not be counted. They would be intentionally left out of the census, and the communities they live in could lose representation and federal funding.1 The Constitution already answered this question. The census counts the "whole number of persons in each state." Just this June, the Supreme Court turned back an attempt to restrict birthright citizenship. This proposal recycles many of the same arguments.1 This is the thousand-cuts pattern again: another attempt to shrink the definition of who belongs here and leave millions of working people uncounted and unheard. So on this Citizenship Day, we keep pushing for a country that sees all of us. We want a country where our neighbors are counted, not erased. We want one where the people who keep this country running have a permanent home. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | In solidarity, Aria, United We Dream * 1. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: New Medicare for All polling ➡️
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Working families are not confused about universal healthcare — they need Congress to have the courage to take action.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260917-6731-footer&t=1&akid=6731%2E420207%2E_b6z4t)
Peter,
I have some incredibly exciting news to share!
My Medicare for All PAC just commissioned **new independent polling** — and the results are in:
📈 94% of Democrats agree, it’s time to make Medicare for All a reality!
📈 60% support among swing voters.
📈 67% support among moderates.
📈 Even 1 in 5 Republicans and Trump voters support Medicare for All.
**Overall support is at a resounding 60% majority of voters, up from 54% in the last poll we did in December of 2025.**
The most powerful part? Even when we stress-tested some of the most common arguments against Medicare for All, including cost and taxes going up, _support for Medicare for All stayed strong._
**That is because working families have seen their healthcare collapse; they’re paying $25,000 a year just for their insurance premiums (!) and medical debt is soaring.**
We are sick of worrying about losing healthcare if you lose your job.
We are sick of some corporate insurer deciding which doctor you can see.
We are sick of paying more and getting less.
70% of people now disapprove of for-profit insurance companies. Four in ten people surveyed have been denied coverage by their insurance, and one in four face a medical debt of over $1,000. One in three are paying more than $500 a month for healthcare.
**Let me be clear: the American people are _not_ confused about Medicare for All. **
They know what it’s like to skip a doctor’s visit because the copay is too high, or ration medication because the prescription costs more than a week of groceries. Working families have been living with this broken, for-profit healthcare system their entire lives.
**They don’t need to be convinced — they need us to have the courage to take action.**
This is not a fringe idea. This is what working families need and deserve. We’re going full speed ahead to deliver it, and momentum is on our side.
**The numbers show Medicare for All is _not_ a political liability. It’s our strength. **
That’s exactly why my Medicare for All PAC has been investing in candidates across the country who will fight for it in Congress, because taking back the House and building towards a Democratic trifecta is how we turn our vision into law.
We have a clear vision of what we’re fighting for, a real plan to get there, and an unstoppable movement. We will not stop fighting until every single person in this country can see a doctor without going broke. That’s my commitment, and it always has been.
But I need this people-powered movement standing with me to carry on this fight in Congress.
[**If you can, will you please pitch in $3, or whatever is meaningful to you today to help me keep fighting to make Medicare for All a reality for every person in this country?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260917-1.A0IfhI&refcode=em20260917-6731&amount=3&t=2&akid=6731%2E420207%2E_b6z4t)

Thank you,

That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Peter, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Peter: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Peter. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Peter: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Fellow Conservative: In 1991, the mob came for Clarence Thomas. They smeared him. They tried to destroy his name, his reputation, and his honor. As Justice Thomas himself has put it, critics in Washington _"don't bomb you, necessarily, but they bomb your reputation or your good name or your honor."_ **He refused to cave.** And because he did, he became one of the four giants of the modern Supreme Court — alongside Justices Scalia, Alito, and Rehnquist. Senator Ted Cruz has just released a remarkable new book: _**Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas**_ , built on exclusive interviews with the Justice himself.

---
|
---
[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=0a308ab9f4a240b1b023ca192d7c99d5&_e=ALuhi4L0IKWgDYU4W5NFZZLb-BQz_QR-QDwXbK35sVUb3k0GD309Uw144aMk9YBwSj3_eA0xa45u9qPykN8DIC1RuVjaa7_9vHknjAVQufF2idQgFMQ0oxfGktTyn7hdMVYqkGhTiNUnbM6r4F78EM8KJtqg04K0qMN53JDLjMcToBcepalubS8Fegvpa7rQrGPN49n_A1R0o1OyBbavKCXERctGu3cUS925-_1U4rWV7taBMKO83EDJPpWc_75xea_L8U35140VRfBKvie16MLabLZ95vKRspPAOIHeMtiYbrb62W3Wh7MMueLZHV0L3I2at2030fycNZwK3yTjQx0ihgMbCbJzUkBbQJVw9DOr1wsUbrmaHxosgFz09836mkN1B1PhZ8hLemdDeQAQ9w%3D%3D)
---
|
---
It tells the story of a man who rose from grinding poverty in Pin Point, Georgia — raised by a grandfather he calls _"the single greatest human being I've ever met"_ — to become, in Cruz's words, the justice _"more willing to go back to the original Constitution... and to overturn precedent" than any other in history._

There's a moment in the book that says everything. When Justice Scalia told Thomas he was _"tilting at windmills"_ by trying to overturn bad precedent, Thomas shot back: _"Nino, windmills are dangerous."_

That is the kind of courage we need on the federal bench. And here is the part every conservative must understand:

**Clarence Thomas only reached the Supreme Court because the Senate confirmed him by just two votes.**

Presidents nominate judges. But the Senate confirms them. Every originalist on the bench, and every one we hope to see there, depends on having conservative senators willing to fight. When we lose the Senate, we lose the courts. It's that simple.

That's the mission of the Senate Conservatives Fund: electing principled conservatives to the U.S. Senate so we can confirm the next generation of Clarence Thomases, and stop the Left from ever again turning a confirmation hearing into a character assassination.

So today, we want to put Senator Cruz's book in your hands.

Clarence Thomas went further. Now it's our turn.

[**Contribute $50 or more and get your copy of _Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas_.**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=0a308ab9f4a240b1b023ca192d7c99d5&_e=ALuhi4L0IKWgDYU4W5NFZZLb-BQz_QR-QDwXbK35sVUb3k0GD309Uw144aMk9YBwSj3_eA0xa45u9qPykN8DIC1RuVjaa7_9vHknjAVQufHXT4SZ9VQ5-gfeqB1sB28617UnhkyAvSQoPxlnai1JGIMFuGNwxQnKJFpl95v0bmF1TdxiF0-Yc6wyorzseyyOr2oC2AMtI3Rt5OBYy-fVaYxauM0i7Yo5fg07HkbRNn23YKUyzNMK7EMBAhG6t4vEZa8TzMtaZVzTYqJLzadVJkxLVc7UsLIa-4rbPlFT57ZLXhF_mWNulpQD_1dCfUOG5Eh1JHSzE57jeDa1ZBFuhT8RqpPbpdLFQGGsj-n6jrHnJHm2ixa8Fmv4KqWxii5wI16hZkIe2zYmQ6k7ly2oag%3D%3D) It's a win-win. You will help elect strong conservative U.S. Senate candidates, and you will get a hardcover copy of this best-selling book. Thank you for considering this request and for doing so much to help fight for America's future.

**Boysko Bulletin: ****Early Voting Starts Tomorrow for the 3 Constitutional Amendments and the Congressional Races**** **
---
Dear Peter, Early voting for the November election starts tomorrow, Friday, September 18. All members of the US House of Representatives are up for election and a third of the US Senate. District 38 overlaps two congressional districts - you will see Democrats James Walkinshaw or Donald Beyer on your ballot. You can be sure that they are both fighting for our values and our ability to pay our bills and thrive in our communities. If you live in the Town of Herndon, you will also see town council seats on your ballot. There is also a [Parks and Park Facilities bond issue question and a Community Health and Human Services Facilities bond issue question](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421157/647295396/-150005810?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556). ** ** This year, all Virginia voters will have [three Virginia Constitutional Amendments](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421158/647295397/-968106734?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556) for consideration. I urge you to vote yes if you agree that we should have:
* Freedom to decide for yourself about reproductive health with the advice and care from your doctor - not politicians;
* Freedom to marry the person you love without government interference;
* Freedom to vote and to be treated as a full-fledged citizen with the same rights and responsibilities as other Virginians after completing your incarceration when you return to the community.

Want to vote on the first day of early voting? Join me at [**THE JOY OF VOTING -- LETS DO IT TOGETHER IN FAIRFAX September 18th**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421159/647295398/216975177?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556) from 10:30 to 11:30 am at the Fairfax County Government Center. Kindest regards,

**Legislative Updates** Work continues on my 2027 Session Legislative Slate. I have requested drafts for 9 bills so far - tackling criminal justice reform, support for teachers, employment discrimination, healthcare access, and housing affordability. Now I share the bills with advocates and identify stakeholders, including those who may not support the legislation, and work with them over the next few months. My schedule is filled with meetings with advocates and other stakeholders.. Our bill limit will be 15 bills plus an additional 5 if we requested the drafts by August 31 which I did. Once my legislation is drafted and changes made, I will file it and you will find the bills on [lis.virginia.gov](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421161/647295400/303244636?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556) \- this is [my page](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421162/647295401/-124516961?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556). I also have the opportunity to recognize members of our community for their accomplishments - please let me know if there is someone you would like to receive a commendation or memorial resolution. To submit ideas for legislation, please email senatorboysko@senate.virginia.gov. **Continue the Fight Against Tysons Casino Legislation** Governor Spanberger vetoed the 2026 Session casino legislation,****[SB 756](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421163/647295402/-1821246626?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556), and the Senate sustained the veto by voting to pass the bill by for the day. In meetings with the Governor’s team, they mentioned the many emails you all sent. We have made it clear that our community does not want a casino, would not benefit from a casino financially, and in fact would be harmed by a casino. Despite the clear rejection of our community, sponsors of the legislation have vowed to introduce the bill again so we will continue the fight. All of you who oppose this proposal should stay engaged. By organizing, educating our neighbors, and reaching out to state leaders, we have made sure that our concerns were heard loud and clear and we will continue that work. You can sign up for updates, and take action, visit the [No Fairfax Casino coalition](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421164/647295403/-833915805?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556). Together, we can continue building momentum and strengthen the No Tysons Casino movement. **Election Updates Including Early Voting** Worried about the actions of the federal government on our elections? Here’s an article on steps you can take to ensure that your vote counts. [**5 Quick Steps To Protect Your Right To Vote**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421165/647295404/-1119575108?utm_medium=email&_hsenc=p2ANqtz-9Qsnq6vPYpn3xPcuz9DpnTOSFcUQstsGUH8TC51iGQU0-86xVimKTyf4hC_w6ta1Fj1yyIP40IhZTocOcz1kpQnwcItf62HpxCGhukQe_haxKyino&_hsmi=438465629&utm_content=438465629&utm_source=hs_email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556)**; As misinformation and confusion about election integrity continue to spread, citizens can work to strengthen American democracy by focusing on what matters most—that individuals are ready to vote.**(author Ben Hovland, Center for American Progress) As the former chairman of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission, I have traveled across the country to observe election administration and speak with the public servants who run elections. Although each state has its own laws and procedures, some principles are consistent nationwide: Election officials are professionals, they follow state and federal law, and transparency is built into the process. These safeguards should give Americans confidence in elections. Unfortunately, some foreign and domestic actors seek to spread doubt and confusion about the democratic process and discourage people from voting. These tactics also establish a pretext to claim results are untrustworthy. Such efforts are favored by antidemocratic actors because it makes the electoral process appear less desirable and eases the pathway to grab power. There is, however, a great way for voters to push back on such efforts: be engaged and undeterred. If the goal is to discourage Americans from participating, that backfires when large numbers show up to exercise their right to vote. Fortunately, all Americans can take basic steps to help ensure their vote counts, the process works well for voters and election workers, and our democracy better reflects the country as a whole. Here are five steps Americans should take to be ready for the upcoming midterms and every election.
1. Check your voter registration and make sure it is current. Every state except North Dakota requires voters to register. Deadlines vary, though none may be more than 30 days before Election Day. Many Americans forget to update their registration or reregister after moving, which can create problems at the polls or prevent them from voting.
2. Learn your voting options. Most states allow voters to cast a ballot early in person, by mail, or on Election Day. Knowing the options in your state—and choosing what works best for your schedule—will help ensure you can participate.
3. Make a plan to vote. Because each state offers different options for casting a ballot, decide which option works best for you and know when and how you will vote. If you plan to vote early in person, find your early voting location and set aside time to go. If you plan to vote by mail, learn how to request a ballot and return it early enough to meet all deadlines.
4. Do not wait. If you know who you are voting for, cast your ballot as soon as you are ready. Early in-person voting and other options add resilience to the election process. If something unexpected comes up, whether that is with your voter record or simply because life gets busy, voting early gives you more time and options. Election Day is now the last day to vote—not the only day.
5. Help someone else. Many Americans may already know these steps, but many do not—especially first-time voters or people who have recently moved for school or work. Moving can create extra hurdles that make voting harder. If you have a plan to vote and know someone who may need help, share this list and offer to help them make a plan of their own.

Our democracy is stronger when more Americans can participate, regardless of whom they support. As a voter and citizen, you have a role to play in making sure your voice is heard. If you want to do more, help make sure other Americans’ voices are heard too. ** ****Check Your Registration, Voter Location, Early Voting Hours and More** You can find the election information you need at the [state election website](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421166/647295405/1040056213?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556) or the [Fairfax County election website](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421167/647295406/-150005810?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556). The Fairfax County election website includes information on [early in person voting](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421168/647295407/112561586?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556) and [voting by mail](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421169/647295408/1235618975?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556). Early in person voting starts September 18 with additional locations and hours beginning on October 22. **Three Virginia Constitution Amendments on the November Ballot** **Reproductive Freedom Amendment** The Reproductive Freedom amendment protects access to a broad range of reproductive health care and puts the power where it belongs—with Virginians, their families, and their doctors. No matter your faith or personal beliefs, these are decisions that should be made personally, not by the government. The amendment was crafted to follow the current laws in Virginia, to take the politics out of reproductive healthcare, and to protect the fundamental freedom to make these decisions for ourselves. You are probably aware that the US Supreme Court Dobbs decision removed the fundamental right to privacy regarding abortion, leaving it up to the states. The Constitutional Amendment will guarantee Virginians the fundamental right to reproductive freedom, including the ability to make and carry out decisions relating to one's own prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, contraception, abortion care, miscarriage management, and fertility care. The state would not be allowed to interfere with a person's right to make their own reproductive health choices, for example, by banning certain types of care (like abortion), or making it more difficult to access that care without a strong justification for why doing so would protect patients’ health and safety. The state would still be able to regulate abortion in the third trimester, including by restricting access to the procedure. But the Commonwealth would allow access to abortion, even in the third trimester, where it’s to protect the life or physical or mental health of the pregnant individual or when a fetus is not viable. Virginia would not be allowed to treat people differently from others on the basis of their identity when it comes to protecting or enforcing this basic right. Patients and doctors would be protected from being charged or jailed for accessing or providing reproductive healthcare. Virginia would not be allowed to punish or take action against someone for making their own reproductive healthcare decisions. Virginia also cannot punish someone who helps another person make these choices, as long as the person being helped agrees to it. Virginia would only get involved in someone’s reproductive healthcare choices if it’s necessary to protect or improve the person’s health. Any regulations the Commonwealth imposes on reproductive healthcare, like abortion, must follow trusted medical guidelines and research. The Commonwealth would not take away a person's right to make their own decisions about their body. This language prevents laws that create unnecessary obstacles to abortion care - like “Targeted Restrictions on Abortion Providers” or “TRAP” laws and laws like a 72-hour waiting period or biased counseling before an abortion. The General Assembly passed my legislation twice - once in the 2025 Session and once in the 2026 session. Constitutional amendments require passing the bill in two sessions with an intervening election. Delegate Herring passed identical resolutions. The referendum on the amendment will take place during the November 3 election and all registered voters can vote for or against the amendment. I am working with the [Virginians for Reproductive Freedom](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421170/647295409/-494596654?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556) to encourage people to vote for the amendment. You can also volunteer with Planned Parenthood’s NOVA organizer, Rhea Simon, at [rsimon@ppav.org](mailto:rsimon@ppav.org). Now is the time to act—to secure reproductive freedom for generations to come. **I urge you to vote yes.** **Marriage Amendment** Question 2 would repeal Virginia's 2006 Marshall-Newman Amendment, a ban on marriage between same-sex couples that remains in our Virginia Constitution today, and replace it with an affirmative guarantee that the government must treat all marriages equally under the law. It would enshrine the freedom for adult couples to marry, as the current law in Virginia allows. [Virginians for Marriage Equality](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139421171/647295410/-2015354088?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDI2MjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzM2NDg4ZmUtZTJiMi1mMTExLWE2YTctMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=limJDQzbX8d3U5TdIq4F3unnO82d21cAiOsDf9EWkmo=&emci=391d412a-f1b1-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&emdi=736488fe-e2b2-f111-a6a7-0022482a9a8d&ceid=22486556) is a coalition of Virginia families, couples, faith leaders, and advocacy organizations working to protect the freedom to marry in Virginia. Voters will see Question 2 on their general election ballot: Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) remove the ban on same-sex marriage; (ii) affirm that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, or race; (iii) require all legally valid marriages to be treated equally under the law? As Virginians, we value fairness, dignity, and equal rights. Every Virginian deserves the freedom to marry the person they love, free from government interference. This amendment is simple. It repeals Virginia’s ban on marriages between same-sex couples and ensures every Virginian can marry who they love, free from government interference. This amendment ensures all married couples are protected, no matter what happens at the federal level. Marriage is a fundamental right that provides legal protection, stability, and security. For over a decade, the law on marriage for same-sex couples has been clear, and people have made decisions – bought homes, raised families, built businesses, planned for life – based on it. Virginians shouldn’t have to question whether this right might be taken away in the future. This amendment is about our values. As Virginians, we believe that regardless of who we love, we should be able to live, work, and make deeply personal decisions about our lives with dignity, respect, and equal rights and freedoms. That’s what this amendment is all about. This amendment repeals Virginia's ban on same-sex marriage so Virginians – not politicians – have the freedom to make decisions that are right for themselves. Who you marry is one of the most personal decisions a person can make; the government has no place in deeply personal decisions about love, marriage, and family. This amendment ensures the freedom to marry the person you love is a right enjoyed by every Virginian for generations to come. **I urge you to vote yes.** **Restoration of Rights Amendment** The third Constitutional Amendment that you will see on your ballot pertains to the restoration of rights for returning citizens after completion of their incarceration. It creates an explicit constitutional right to vote for every eligible Virginian, something Virginia’s Constitution does not currently guarantee. Protect against current and future attacks on voting rights by taking the right to vote out of politicians’ hands. Ensure a fair process that doesn’t rely on the whims of politicians by automatically restoring voting rights to Virginians with felony convictions once they have completed their sentences and returned to their communities. The amendment also protects people with disabilities from automatically losing their right to vote when put under a guardianship by empowering judges to decide case-by-case if that person understands the act of voting. Election Updates Including Early Voting Worried about the actions of the federal government on our elections? Here’s an article on steps you can take to ensure that your vote counts. ; As misinformation and confusion about election integrity continue to spread, citizens can work to strengthen American democracy by focusing on what matters most—that individuals are ready to vote.(author Ben Hovland, Center for American Progress) As the former chairman of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission, I have traveled across the country to observe election administration and speak with the public servants who run elections. Although each state has its own laws and procedures, some principles are consistent nationwide: Election officials are professionals, they follow state and federal law, and transparency is built into the process. These safeguards should give Americans confidence in elections. Unfortunately, some foreign and domestic actors seek to spread doubt and confusion about the democratic process and discourage people from voting. These tactics also establish a pretext to claim results are untrustworthy. Such efforts are favored by antidemocratic actors because it makes the electoral process appear less desirable and eases the pathway to grab power. There is, however, a great way for voters to push back on such efforts: be engaged and undeterred. If the goal is to discourage Americans from participating, that backfires when large numbers show up to exercise their right to vote. Fortunately, all Americans can take basic steps to help ensure their vote counts, the process works well for voters and election workers, and our democracy better reflects the country as a whole. Here are five steps Americans should take to be ready for the upcoming midterms and every election. 1. Check your voter registration and make sure it is current. Every state except North Dakota requires voters to register. Deadlines vary, though none may be more than 30 days before Election Day. Many Americans forget to update their registration or reregister after moving, which can create problems at the polls or prevent them from voting. 2. Learn your voting options. Most states allow voters to cast a ballot early in person, by mail, or on Election Day. Knowing the options in your state—and choosing what works best for your schedule—will help ensure you can participate. 3. Make a plan to vote. Because each state offers different options for casting a ballot, decide which option works best for you and know when and how you will vote. If you plan to vote early in person, find your early voting location and set aside time to go. If you plan to vote by mail, learn how to request a ballot and return it early enough to meet all deadlines. 4. Do not wait. If you know who you are voting for, cast your ballot as soon as you are ready. Early in-person voting and other options add resilience to the election process. If something unexpected comes up, whether that is with your voter record or simply because life gets busy, voting early gives you more time and options. Election Day is now the last day to vote—not the only day. 5. Help someone else. Many Americans may already know these steps, but many do not—especially first-time voters or people who have recently moved for school or work. Moving can create extra hurdles that make voting harder. If you have a plan to vote and know someone who may need help, share this list and offer to help them make a plan of their own. Our democracy is stronger when more Americans can participate, regardless of whom they support. As a voter and citizen, you have a role to play in making sure your voice is heard. If you want to do more, help make sure other Americans’ voices are heard too. **Check Your Registration, Voter Location, Early Voting Hours and More You can find the election information you need at the or the . The Fairfax County election website includes information on and . Early in person voting starts September 18 with additional locations and hours beginning on October 22. Three Virginia Constitution Amendments on the November Ballot Reproductive Freedom Amendment The Reproductive Freedom amendment protects access to a broad range of reproductive health care and puts the power where it belongs—with Virginians, their families, and their doctors. No matter your faith or personal beliefs, these are decisions that should be made personally, not by the government. The amendment was crafted to follow the current laws in Virginia, to take the politics out of reproductive healthcare, and to protect the fundamental freedom to make these decisions for ourselves. You are probably aware that the US Supreme Court Dobbs decision removed the fundamental right to privacy regarding abortion, leaving it up to the states. The Constitutional Amendment will guarantee Virginians the fundamental right to reproductive freedom, including the ability to make and carry out decisions relating to one's own prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, contraception, abortion care, miscarriage management, and fertility care. The state would not be allowed to interfere with a person's right to make their own reproductive health choices, for example, by banning certain types of care (like abortion), or making it more difficult to access that care without a strong justification for why doing so would protect patients’ health and safety. The state would still be able to regulate abortion in the third trimester, including by restricting access to the procedure. But the Commonwealth would allow access to abortion, even in the third trimester, where it’s to protect the life or physical or mental health of the pregnant individual or when a fetus is not viable. Virginia would not be allowed to treat people differently from others on the basis of their identity when it comes to protecting or enforcing this basic right. Patients and doctors would be protected from being charged or jailed for accessing or providing reproductive healthcare. Virginia would not be allowed to punish or take action against someone for making their own reproductive healthcare decisions. Virginia also cannot punish someone who helps another person make these choices, as long as the person being helped agrees to it. Virginia would only get involved in someone’s reproductive healthcare choices if it’s necessary to protect or improve the person’s health. Any regulations the Commonwealth imposes on reproductive healthcare, like abortion, must follow trusted medical guidelines and research. The Commonwealth would not take away a person's right to make their own decisions about their body. This language prevents laws that create unnecessary obstacles to abortion care - like “Targeted Restrictions on Abortion Providers” or “TRAP” laws and laws like a 72-hour waiting period or biased counseling before an abortion. The General Assembly passed my legislation twice - once in the 2025 Session and once in the 2026 session. Constitutional amendments require passing the bill in two sessions with an intervening election. Delegate Herring passed identical resolutions. The referendum on the amendment will take place during the November 3 election and all registered voters can vote for or against the amendment. I am working with the to encourage people to vote for the amendment. You can also volunteer with Planned Parenthood’s NOVA organizer, Rhea Simon, at mailto:rsimon@ppav.org. Now is the time to act—to secure reproductive freedom for generations to come. I urge you to vote yes. Marriage Amendment Question 2 would repeal Virginia's 2006 Marshall-Newman Amendment, a ban on marriage between same-sex couples that remains in our Virginia Constitution today, and replace it with an affirmative guarantee that the government must treat all marriages equally under the law. It would enshrine the freedom for adult couples to marry, as the current law in Virginia allows. is a coalition of Virginia families, couples, faith leaders, and advocacy organizations working to protect the freedom to marry in Virginia. Voters will see Question 2 on their general election ballot: Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) remove the ban on same-sex marriage; (ii) affirm that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, or race; (iii) require all legally valid marriages to be treated equally under the law? As Virginians, we value fairness, dignity, and equal rights. Every Virginian deserves the freedom to marry the person they love, free from government interference. This amendment is simple. It repeals Virginia’s ban on marriages between same-sex couples and ensures every Virginian can marry who they love, free from government interference. This amendment ensures all married couples are protected, no matter what happens at the federal level. Marriage is a fundamental right that provides legal protection, stability, and security. For over a decade, the law on marriage for same-sex couples has been clear, and people have made decisions – bought homes, raised families, built businesses, planned for life – based on it. Virginians shouldn’t have to question whether this right might be taken away in the future. This amendment is about our values. As Virginians, we believe that regardless of who we love, we should be able to live, work, and make deeply personal decisions about our lives with dignity, respect, and equal rights and freedoms. That’s what this amendment is all about. This amendment repeals Virginia's ban on same-sex marriage so Virginians – not politicians – have the freedom to make decisions that are right for themselves. Who you marry is one of the most personal decisions a person can make; the government has no place in deeply personal decisions about love, marriage, and family. This amendment ensures the freedom to marry the person you love is a right enjoyed by every Virginian for generations to come. I urge you to vote yes. Restoration of Rights Amendment The third Constitutional Amendment that you will see on your ballot pertains to the restoration of rights for returning citizens after completion of their incarceration. It creates an explicit constitutional right to vote for every eligible Virginian, something Virginia’s Constitution does not currently guarantee. Protect against current and future attacks on voting rights by taking the right to vote out of politicians’ hands. Ensure a fair process that doesn’t rely on the whims of politicians by automatically restoring voting rights to Virginians with felony convictions once they have completed their sentences and returned to their communities. The amendment also protects people with disabilities from automatically losing their right to vote when put under a guardianship by empowering judges to decide case-by-case if that person understands the act of voting. Learn more at . I urge you to vote yes. Herndon Town Council Election Update The mayor and all members of the Herndon Town Council are on the ballot this November. A brand-new poll just showed something that's never happened before.
#
Friends, look at this:
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260917_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.IYCDPB&refcode=em20260917-1715&amount=5&t=1&akid=1715%2E2118727%2EiQpit3)
In his four campaigns for governor, Greg Abbott has never once been shown trailing in a statewide Texas poll. _That changed today._
**A brand-new poll just showed us ahead of Abbott by four points,** while he's asking Texans for a fourth term. Not within range. Not closing the gap. Ahead. For the first time.
Here’s what’s happening: Texans are getting a clear look at what twelve years of Greg Abbott has actually cost them. Rising grocery bills. Rising property taxes. Data centers flooding the state while the people footing the bill get nothing back. And when they look at me, they’re seeing someone who’s spent her career fighting for Texas families — not just for the people at the top.
**None of this happens without you.** We are competitive in this race because of the 170,000 people who've chipped in to build this campaign. Our people-powered movement is working. We are clearly breaking through.
But Abbott has a firehose of money aimed at us — $67 million in the bank, and he's already outspent us 10-to-1. He's never had to run from behind before. With this poll out there, he's going to open that firehose all the way to drown out our campaign before Texans vote.
We can't match him dollar for dollar. But we can outnumber him — that's how we got here. 170,000 donors have helped build this campaign into one that can win.
I’m asking every one of you to dig a little deeper, right now, to keep us competitive.
**[Can you make a donation to my campaign to help us keep building a campaign that can defeat Greg Abbott and take Texas back?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260917_partner_ms_gh_em_leftnet.IYCDPB&refcode=em20260917-1715&amount=5&t=2&akid=1715%2E2118727%2EiQpit3)**

Greg Abbott has never polled behind in a race for governor. Not once. Now that he has, he's going to come at us with everything he's got. We need everything you've got, too.
Gratefully,
Gina

## **Pattern**
**Two institutions. Two domains. One mechanism.**
The first institution was a Republican women's club. They promoted two candidates by name while excluding all others, then claimed neutrality when caught. You trusted that club to be fair. You were denied the information you needed to make an informed choice.
The second was a television station. They excluded the only woman in a five-candidate field from a televised debate, then told you she had not responded to an invitation they never sent. You trusted that station to be neutral. You were denied the opportunity to hear from every candidate.
The club operates in the party infrastructure where you trust your organizations to be fair. The television station operates in the public airwaves where you trust your news sources to be neutral.
The mechanism is the same. This is the predictable operation of the Iron Triangle. Institutions that wish to exclude follow a sequence:
**First, they decide.** Both institutions violated their own standards and made statements that were contradicted by the record.
**Second, they justify.** Both modified their positions after the violation was raised--the club moved through three versions of a promotional post in the three days after the violation was named; the television station's criteria appeared only in a legal response filed after the fact.
**Third, they claim neutrality throughout.** This is the function of this machine's Establishment vertex, acting as a gatekeeper to protect the status quo from any genuine challenge.
**The process is not the "process." The process is the pretext.**
My fellow Americans, this is not a story about a candidate who lost a primary. This is a story about you--a public that lost its voice. You were told by organizations that presented themselves as neutral that certain candidates mattered and others did not. Voters entered the booth on August 18 with information that had been curated. Your consent was presumed. You were never asked.
As we move toward the general election on November 3rd, consider this: the architecture that curated the field in the primary is the same architecture that now frames the choices in the general. The machine that manufactured consent then has not been dismantled. It is the burden of a vigilant public to ensure it does not manufacture consent again.
## **The Iron Triangle in Action**
The exclusion was not a scheduling error. It was a process. The machine that produced it is the Iron Triangle: bureaucracy that writes the rules, establishment that curates who is heard, and special interests that profit from the status those rules protect. The full architecture is set out in _[The Fortress of Power](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/34f02420-9180-45af-acbd-92700faf36b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_. What follows is the machine at work in one primary.
### **LFRWC: The Club 's Promotional Posts**
**What Was Published**
On August 3, 2026, I observed the Lake Federated Republican Women's Club (LFRWC) published a promotional post on their Facebook page for their August 12 meeting. The post read: "From Congressional District 11, meet Candidates Carey Baker and Tim Wilkins."
Two candidates. Named specifically. Promoted as featured speakers. No invitation to the other candidates. No indication that any candidate outside the chosen two was welcome.
**The Bylaws They Wrote**
The club's own bylaws forbid it.
* Article III, Section 1.a is explicit: the organization "shall not publicly endorse any candidate for public office in contested Republican primaries."
* Section 1.f adds the condition of fairness: clubs may distribute candidate information "if they are fair and distribute equally for all."

By naming two candidates and excluding the others, the original post was in clear violation of these provisions.
**What Their Responses Revealed**
When the discrepancy was raised, the club's responses showed contradictions in their public statements.
On August 3, a club representative texted that speakers were "selected months in advance by our second vice president." The very next day, a different representative sent an email that denied the premise of the first claim. This new version asserted the candidates had "contacted the Club and requested an opportunity to speak," directly contradicting the initial story that the club had selected them.
**Two statements. Two contradictions. One institution.**
That representative also claimed that "no candidate is being endorsed or given preferential treatment" and that the meeting is "a regularly scheduled club business meeting, not a candidate forum or debate." Yet the original post had named specific candidates as featured speakers.
After the discrepancy was raised, the club revised its promotional post twice within four days. The initial post named specific candidates and included their campaign messages. A later version removed the names and invited the previously excluded candidates. But the advantage of preferential treatment had already been conferred. And it was only after repeated requests that equal time was assured.
**What Was Betrayed**
The club's bylaws demand neutrality. Its actions betrayed them. The public trusted the club to be fair, but voters were denied the information they needed to make an informed choice. When partisan organizations create preferential treatment for preferred candidates, they do more than exclude a contender. They undermine the very principles they claim to uphold: fair competition, merit, and equal treatment. These values protect your right to choose. When this structure operates within the party, it does not strengthen it. It hollows.
And those who depend on these values pay the price. They begin to question the party's legitimacy and, worse, their own convictions. This harm defies measurement, potentially fracturing the bonds that allow families to stand, to choose, to resist. Broken trust is the cost of autonomy in the face of a machine that governs without consent.
**Strike the root. Secure the table.**

Although his latest attempt to bend USPS mail-in ballot regulations in his favor was blocked by the U.S. Supreme Court, there’s no telling what other tricks he’ll try to pull before this Election Day or in future elections. So why is he doing this now? Context is important, Peter. Gas prices are up. Food prices are up. He got us into a war nobody wants. He’s worried he is going to lose the midterm elections. * * *
Hey folks,
[Jack Cocchiarella](https://open.substack.com/pub/jackcocchiarella?utm_source=mentions) and I are finally back together, and we had a lot to get off our chests.
We get into Joe Rogan's latest comments about Trump supporters, what Republican spending is telling us about the midterms, and the bigger problem underneath all of it: a political system that protects insiders while millions of people are asking why nothing ever seems to get better.
* [**00:03:10**] Joe Rogan turns on Trump supporters again--and Jack asks why it took him this long to see what was happening.
* [**00:07:18**] We get into the danger of treating politicians like saviors and why public officials should remember they work for actual people.
* [**00:12:38**] Mitch McConnell becomes the clearest example of our bigger argument: Washington protects its own, even when the public deserves answers.
* [**00:17:31**] We talk about the media's handling of McConnell, the lack of transparency around his public appearances, and why accountability matters.
* [**00:23:49**] We bring it all home: people are struggling economically, the system keeps rewarding insiders, and tinkering around the edges isn't enough anymore.

Politics should be about improving people's lives, not preserving somebody's place in the club. We need institutions that answer to people, leaders willing to use their power for good, and media willing to keep asking uncomfortable questions. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: I am calling for an immediate pause in advanced AI development:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3025%2E4032634%2EmDBdtb)
---
I want to be very clear about the conversations surrounding AI right now. **Before I get into explanation mode, let me just start at the top: I am calling for an immediate pause in advanced AI development.** It’s clear that frontier AI models are a dangerous technology without the safeguards needed to protect people from serious harm. But the recent calls by AI industry leaders to “pace the frontier” are insufficient. And their suggestions that we must weaken antitrust protections in order to confront the AI threat are transparently self-serving. The future of this technology should be determined by the American people through their democratically elected representatives in government — not by a handful of CEOs and billionaire corporations. So I’m calling for this pause while lawmakers and regulators create systems to keep people safe, and for Congress to urgently pass legislation to put stronger guardrails in place before we have a cyberattack, economic crisis, or national security disaster facilitated by AI. [**Add your name if you’re with me: Now is the moment to demand that Congress steps up to regulate AI and protect people.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-pause-ai/?source=EW_EMZ33O_AAI_ENG_20260917_F&t=8&akid=3025%2E4032634%2EmDBdtb) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-pause-ai/?source=EW_EMZ33O_AAI_ENG_20260917_F&t=9&akid=3025%2E4032634%2EmDBdtb)
---
Before these recent warnings, tech executives were warning that AI could lead to “a level of wealth concentration that will break society” and create a "permanent underclass."
Their words.
This technology has created dozens of tech billionaires while companies lay off workers in the name of AI. And data centers are jacking up electricity bills for nearby families — costs have skyrocketed by as much as 267% over the past five years.
I’ve been advocating for Congress to do something about these threats. I proposed legislation that would tax these AI companies to give us resources to invest in things like free college and apprenticeship programs, a jobs guarantee, and universal health care so we can avoid this "permanent underclass” they’re promising.
I’ve demanded that AI companies take ownership of the enormous energy costs their data centers are causing.
The recent warnings have made it abundantly clear: The time for the government to act on AI was yesterday. So I’ve called for this immediate pause on advanced AI development.
If we had a competent President who didn’t curry favor with corporate interests at every turn, the U.S. would lead the world in setting the rules of AI and make sure the safety of humanity is the top priority, not the profits of a handful of multi-billion-dollar companies.
We can’t just accept this as our reality, and we can’t trust AI executives alone to regulate themselves. It’s time for the government to intervene to keep people safe.
[**Let’s make this loud and clear: the people are demanding an immediate pause in AI development — and it’s on Congress to act. Add your name to show your support.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-pause-ai/?source=EW_EMZ33O_AAI_ENG_20260917_F&t=10&akid=3025%2E4032634%2EmDBdtb)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

Michigan Republican Senate candidate at the 2026 Republican National Convention at the American Airlines Center on September 10, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images.
_Story by Tom Perkins_
Over 400 alleged Michigan Jewish Democratic and independent voters signed a [pledge in late August](https://substack.com/redirect/c9a055b5-5c27-437b-acdb-f48e4b4611bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to vote for Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers, igniting a controversy and generating questions about whether Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed was losing critical support among a group that typically votes blue by about a 2:1 ratio.
But a Drop Site review of signatories in the "[Michigan Jews Against Extremism](https://substack.com/redirect/c9a055b5-5c27-437b-acdb-f48e4b4611bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" campaign finds many of the Jewish community leaders involved have deep ties to the GOP, as well as to pro-Israel activist groups such as AIPAC. Nearly 50 were involved in a nearly identical gambit in 2012 that went by the name "Jews for Mitt." Then-President Barack Obama, the group argued, was so "anti-Israel" that their consciences drove them to abandon the Democratic Party to support Republican nominee Mitt Romney.
Among those who signed both the Romney and Rogers pledges are six members of the Schostaks, a politically powerful family behind a major Michigan development company. Bobby Schostak, the former head of the Michigan Republican Party, signed the Jews For Mitt pledge, but this time did not pretend to be a Democrat--he now serves as the Rogers campaign's finance chair.
Dozens of signatories either work with the GOP, have served in office as Republicans, have run as Republicans, or donate to right-wing candidates, including Donald Trump.
The operation, however, has been extraordinarily effective, garnering enormous media attention, which frames the group as genuine Democrats who were finally pushed over the edge by El-Sayed.
Taken together, nearly 90% of the first 430 signatories are either connected to pro-Israel activist groups, GOP aligned, Jews for Mitt voters, or may not live in Michigan.
