The Michigan Jews campaign appears to be an "astroturf operation" led by AIPAC and other Republican-affiliated activists, said Jess Newman, a former special assistant for AIPAC's vice CEO. She now works with the Democratic Socialists of America.
Many of the top signatories are well-known Jewish community leaders, Newman added, and the campaign seeks to "create a permission structure to vote for Rogers" for less politically active Democratic Jews who do not know that most of these leaders are connected to Republicans, or are Republicans.
"They are using this brazen tactic because they know that people aren't going to look deeply into it, and some Jewish voters will say 'Oh, I recognize a few names on this list so I can find a way to hold my nose and vote for the Republican," Newman said. "The implication is that this is a list of Democrats who otherwise would vote for Democrats, had a red line not been crossed."
The campaign's website states, "Many of us have been fiercely supportive of Democratic candidates and principles." But FEC records show many signatories have donated to GOP candidates, including Trump, Rick Snyder, Kelly Loeffler, Marco Rubio, Mike Lee, Rick Santorum, the Republican National Congressional Committee, and PACs that support a wide range of Republican candidates, including GOP Michigan House Leader Matt Hall.
Among the signatories are current and former leadership for AIPAC, as well as groups that have led the charge against pro-Palestinian advocates in Michigan and nationally, including the Jewish Federation, Hillel, and Anti-Defamation League.
Drop Site did not include in its 90% figure people who simply are connected with a Jewish communal group, or a synagogue not involved in Israel activism. However, it did include those in leadership at synagogues Adot Shalom and Shaarey Zedek, which [openly](https://substack.com/redirect/7a4e9e45-81c1-45df-88d5-c60ed73fc0ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [work with AIPAC](https://substack.com/redirect/c01c08a4-8f40-4f22-8c7a-09e291ee7976?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), support the IDF, and make pro-Israel activism a central component of their mission.
The list's first signer is Adam Kaplan, a Hillel donor, AIPAC donor, former Jewish Federation committee member, and an [appointee](https://substack.com/redirect/55323ea4-4986-42a5-aa3d-bb7a28ca7dcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the administration of Republican former Michigan Gov. Rick Snyder.
Some signatories have run for office as Republicans, including Bubba Urdan, a West Bloomfield resident who [ran for the GOP nomination](https://substack.com/redirect/03310a51-0d9c-4bc6-a1af-cfd60ec3d2f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Michigan state house, and has served on Jewish Federation boards. Urdan did not respond to a request for comment.
A spokesperson for Michigan Jews Against Extremism said the letter "was not organized by AIPAC or in coordination with it or any other organization." She did not address questions about the Republican ties.
The signatories' AIPAC-GOP connections run deep. Among them is David Handelman, a Mitch McConnell [donor](https://substack.com/redirect/b99407cc-0346-4005-abc9-99eb10575ae9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and former AIPAC Michigan president who once [organized a Detroit pro-Israel event](https://substack.com/redirect/222a18fe-5df0-4d11-9109-67ad1cb2a52e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the 2002 Iraq War architect and diplomat John Bolton as the featured speaker.
Former [AIPAC national president](https://substack.com/redirect/c2a1dc57-dc48-43dd-887b-26ffcff21002?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) David Victor still sits on its national board, and donated to Mike Rogers in 2010. He also [donated to](https://substack.com/redirect/a4231e1b-5fb3-4bc8-a693-b5ad6bec177f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) John McCain and GOP Ohio Congress members John Boehner and Rob Portman, as well as many Democrats.
Max Newman is a metro Detroit attorney and AIPAC activist who also works with Hillel. Campaign finance [records show](https://substack.com/redirect/f3b3a1a1-3f79-4b7d-bdb5-f60e0e92644c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he donated to Rogers multiple times in the aughts, Rudy Giuliani, the National Republican Congressional Committee and many Democrats.
Joshua Opperer is the [executive director of AIPAC's National New Leaders Network](https://substack.com/redirect/20e14e5d-c1dd-4789-84dd-df78c8826e12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and Jewish Federation of Detroit's [executive committee](https://substack.com/redirect/3c568ce6-2489-4b01-a5a3-4513e50babe5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recently [donated $10,000](https://substack.com/redirect/64d337bd-f122-4925-ab96-58e4fd4a7368?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to AIPAC, and published a Substack article titled, "Fireworks in Rafah," that includes a picture of Israeli soldiers celebrating Israel's independence day by lighting off fireworks in Rafah. He has [donated](https://substack.com/redirect/6a619bf3-f2b2-46d3-95ee-554aaeb6b4d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to several Republicans, as well as Democrats.
The 2012 Jews For Mitt [ad declares](https://substack.com/redirect/e8fac6fd-b3fb-4e7a-94a3-f33a79b4a707?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "We are Michigan Jews. Four years ago many of us voted for Barack Obama. Today we are voting for Mitt Romney." The ad alleges Obama had "anti-Israel policies," and claims Mitt Romney would "aggressively combat Muslim extremism" and "fortify America's crucial relationship with Israel."
Among the 49 people who are a part of both campaigns are the Schostacks, Urdan, Max Newman, Victor, and Handelman, who are all Republicans or have donated to Republicans. It includes many other AIPAC activists, like Margo Woll.
"They are dusting off their old strategy of trying to create a grass-tops campaign that makes it look like Jewish people in general are not going to vote for the Democratic nominee," said former Democrat Congress member Andy Levin, who was defeated in a 2022 election bid by the AIPAC-backed Haley Stevens in a metro Detroit district. Only about one-third of Michigan Jews are Republican, Levin said, and he believes most Jews will still vote for El-Sayed.
The campaign spokesperson told Drop Site, "For some signatories, our concern is much more personal: as Jews we do not feel safe when political rhetoric minimizes antisemitism, excuses or contextualizes violence against Jews, or embraces an agenda we believe is hostile to our community, our safety and our children's safety."
"We are speaking for ourselves, exercising our right as Michigan voters, and asking to be heard without being reduced to a political label."
Among those who do not appear to live in Michigan is Hannan Lis, who [told Detroit ABC affiliate ](https://substack.com/redirect/fa9489db-3f85-4a88-aa9e-95b90eb33978?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[WXYZ](https://substack.com/redirect/fa9489db-3f85-4a88-aa9e-95b90eb33978?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ in March that he moved to Israel several years ago to be closer to his grandkids, and who has been described as an "Israeli citizen" in older media reports. He was [part of](https://substack.com/redirect/4cbd9f68-b05b-4d12-8074-b8b58b32ce86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Jewish Federation's board of governors and the AIPAC National Council. Lis told Drop Site he is a dual citizen who splits time between Israel and Michigan. He is registered to vote in Michigan.
"The key question here is 'Who speaks for the Jews and who are the Jews?'" said Levin, a former Michigan synagogue president.
"This idea that these right wing-on-Israel groups are the Jewish people or they represent the Jewish people is just demonstrably false," Levin added. He said there is an intense organizing effort in Michigan's Jewish community for El-Sayed, but the media and the vast amount of attention goes to a statistically small number of voters who are pledging to cast a ballot for Rogers.
Levin's father, former Rep. Sandy Levin, 95, who served as the powerful chair of the House Ways and Means Committee, [made an unusual foray back into politics](https://substack.com/redirect/f395afe4-595d-468c-a1d7-7e4b139ae6a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to endorse El-Sayed this week. On Wednesday, a list of over 600 Michigan Jews pledging to support El-Sayed was released.
Jewish voters make up about 1% of Michigan's electorate, and right-wing Jewish voters may represent as little as .3% of voters statewide. The number of Democrats who may switch is even more miniscule within the context of the state's electorate. That raises questions about the outsize media attention to this tiny group of voters, Levin said.
Some on the list, and some Jewish Democrats, genuinely may not be able to vote for El-Sayed, Jess Newman said. She added that the campaign is "preying on latent Islamophobia."
"It's about depressing voter turnout for El-Sayed and getting people on the margins, and if they have to lie to get there, then they will," Newman added.

However, it did include those in leadership at synagogues Adot Shalom and Shaarey Zedek, which , support the IDF, and make pro-Israel activism a central component of their mission. The list's first signer is Adam Kaplan, a Hillel donor, AIPAC donor, former Jewish Federation committee member, and an in the administration of Republican former Michigan Gov. Rick Snyder. Some signatories have run for office as Republicans, including Bubba Urdan, a West Bloomfield resident who in the Michigan state house, and has served on Jewish Federation boards. Urdan did not respond to a request for comment. A spokesperson for Michigan Jews Against Extremism said the letter "was not organized by AIPAC or in coordination with it or any other organization." She did not address questions about the Republican ties. The signatories' AIPAC-GOP connections run deep. Among them is David Handelman, a Mitch McConnell and former AIPAC Michigan president who once with the 2002 Iraq War architect and diplomat John Bolton as the featured speaker. Former David Victor still sits on its national board, and donated to Mike Rogers in 2010. He also John McCain and GOP Ohio Congress members John Boehner and Rob Portman, as well as many Democrats. Max Newman is a metro Detroit attorney and AIPAC activist who also works with Hillel. Campaign finance he donated to Rogers multiple times in the aughts, Rudy Giuliani, the National Republican Congressional Committee and many Democrats. Joshua Opperer is the and Jewish Federation of Detroit's recently to AIPAC, and published a Substack article titled, "Fireworks in Rafah," that includes a picture of Israeli soldiers celebrating Israel's independence day by lighting off fireworks in Rafah. He has to several Republicans, as well as Democrats. The 2012 Jews For Mitt "We are Michigan Jews. Four years ago many of us voted for Barack Obama. Today we are voting for Mitt Romney." The ad alleges Obama had "anti-Israel policies," and claims Mitt Romney would "aggressively combat Muslim extremism" and "fortify America's crucial relationship with Israel." Among the 49 people who are a part of both campaigns are the Schostacks, Urdan, Max Newman, Victor, and Handelman, who are all Republicans or have donated to Republicans. It includes many other AIPAC activists, like Margo Woll. "They are dusting off their old strategy of trying to create a grass-tops campaign that makes it look like Jewish people in general are not going to vote for the Democratic nominee," said former Democrat Congress member Andy Levin, who was defeated in a 2022 election bid by the AIPAC-backed Haley Stevens in a metro Detroit district. Only about one-third of Michigan Jews are Republican, Levin said, and he believes most Jews will still vote for El-Sayed. The campaign spokesperson told Drop Site, "For some signatories, our concern is much more personal: as Jews we do not feel safe when political rhetoric minimizes antisemitism, excuses or contextualizes violence against Jews, or embraces an agenda we believe is hostile to our community, our safety and our children's safety." "We are speaking for ourselves, exercising our right as Michigan voters, and asking to be heard without being reduced to a political label." Among those who do not appear to live in Michigan is Hannan Lis, who in March that he moved to Israel several years ago to be closer to his grandkids, and who has been described as an "Israeli citizen" in older media reports. He was the Jewish Federation's board of governors and the AIPAC National Council. Lis told Drop Site he is a dual citizen who splits time between Israel and Michigan. He is registered to vote in Michigan. "The key question here is 'Who speaks for the Jews and who are the Jews?'" said Levin, a former Michigan synagogue president. "This idea that these right wing-on-Israel groups are the Jewish people or they represent the Jewish people is just demonstrably false," Levin added. He said there is an intense organizing effort in Michigan's Jewish community for El-Sayed, but the media and the vast amount of attention goes to a statistically small number of voters who are pledging to cast a ballot for Rogers. Levin's father, former Rep. Sandy Levin, 95, who served as the powerful chair of the House Ways and Means Committee, to endorse El-Sayed this week. On Wednesday, a list of over 600 Michigan Jews pledging to support El-Sayed was released. Jewish voters make up about 1% of Michigan's electorate, and right-wing Jewish voters may represent as little as .3% of voters statewide. The number of Democrats who may switch is even more miniscule within the context of the state's electorate. That raises questions about the outsize media attention to this tiny group of voters, Levin said. Some on the list, and some Jewish Democrats, genuinely may not be able to vote for El-Sayed, Jess Newman said. She added that the campaign is "preying on latent Islamophobia." "It's about depressing voter turnout for El-Sayed and getting people on the margins, and if they have to lie to get there, then they will," Newman added. Two stories ran on the New York Post's business page on September 15 (https://nypost.com/2026/09/15/business/google-deepmind-researcher-quits-with-chilling-ai-warning-it-could-kill-us-all/) that belong stapled together. In one, a Google DeepMind researcher quits and warns that artificial intelligence could "kill us all." In the other, the man positioning himself as our best protection against exactly that -- Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei -- has handpicked his own AI watchdog from inside a small, ideologically uniform movement with deep financial and professional ties to the industry it audits. Read together, they sketch a genuinely strange moment: the people inside the labs say the machines may end the world, and the people appointed to check the labs all worked at the same companies, attended the same conferences, and draw money from the same philanthropic well.

My honest answer? **"It sucked."** The other incoming freshmen around me already had their races called. They were celebrating, meeting colleagues, and learning how to set up their offices. Then there was me. I was just the member-elect. Maybe. Because nobody knew if I’d actually won yet. It could still go either way. In fact, for the first three days of orientation, **I was still trailing.** I was sitting in official briefings, taking notes on House procedure, all while checking my phone under the desk to see if our team in Orange County had made up any ground. It wasn’t until a few days later in D.C. that I finally took the lead. By about 17 votes. And even after orientation ended, I still had another two weeks of waiting. It took **22 days** after Election Day for the race to finally be called. In the end, we won by 653 votes. I'm telling you this now because we're right back in it. The only way we’ll get fresh ideas is by electing leaders who will actually fight for them.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41577%2E3422442%2EiD9Vio)
Dear Peter,
Last week, I was on _Lovett or Leave It_ with Jon Lovett, part of Pod Save America media. [About 5 minutes into our interview](https://act.katieporter.com/go/22220?t=2&akid=41577%2E3422442%2EiD9Vio), after I had given a spirited explanation of the causes and consequences of Democrats failing to advance actual policy ideas, Jon Lovett looked at me and said:
**_“You are just bursting at the seams. You are bored at home with your books.”_**
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260917_1_ak.qI2Qbm&refcode=em20260917-41577&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41577%2E3422442%2EiD9Vio)
I love reading for pleasure (you can check out more on my book account, [@KatiePorterTurnsThePage](https://act.katieporter.com/go/22221?t=4&akid=41577%2E3422442%2EiD9Vio)), and I love being a Professor of Law at UC Irvine, which involves reading _a lot_ of books. But he had a point. I am bursting at the seams for change. I want:
* A better democracy, including campaign finance reform,
* Less corruption, including a ban on congressional stock trading and ethics rules for the Supreme Court (and others!),
* An economy that will allow today’s kids to find meaning, and income, from their work,
* A slowing (heck, a complete stop!) from climate change and its harms, and
* No more Donald Trump. And certainly not in the White House.

To accomplish these goals, I want to hear **ideas**. Politicians are trained to parrot the problems of their constituents. It makes us sound relatable, and to be fair, many of the problems (like what job market will my college-aged kid find in a year, given AI) were actual problems in my life—but I think _you know what your problems are._
**What you would like, if you are anything like me, is some solution to those problems.** That means actual policy ideas. Not all of them will be sound or feasible, but as I told Jon Lovett, the lack of imagination from Democratic leaders about policy solutions and implementation is pretty shocking.
The only way we’ll get fresh ideas is by electing leaders who will actually fight for them. **That's why I’m supporting a slate of candidates running to bring bold change to Congress** —including several in must-win races.
If we’re going to actually help working families, we need these candidates to flip Congress and expand our political imagination.
Helping us support them is one of the most important ways you can move our party and our country forward. We can win, but only if we work together.
**[Can you help us bring exciting new ideas to Washington by pitching in $5 to Truth to Power today? Your donation will give us the resources to boost these candidates where it matters most.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260917_1_ak.qI2Qbm&refcode=em20260917-41577&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=41577%2E3422442%2EiD9Vio)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260917_1_ak.qI2Qbm&refcode=em20260917-41577&t=24&akid=41577%2E3422442%2EiD9Vio)
Thank you,
Katie Porter

Team: The Supreme Court dropped another "shadow docket" ruling last night, finally blocking**Trump and the USPS from implementing his anti-mail-in voting Executive Order**. For the midterms, at least. Again, if this is new for you: **The "_shadow docket_."** It's the Supreme Court's way to review cases quickly without formal hearings. It's a construct of the last few decades, not widely used before then, but tons of unsigned, pro-Trump rulings have been issued from the Supreme Court this way the last few years. This was another ruling offered on _procedural grounds_ and not the merits of the law. **The 7-2 decision will stop the Department of Homeland Security and the Postal Service from creating a national voter registration list** and usurping the constitutional authority of the states to run our elections. clean_body: CNBC: Trump calls Supreme Court mail ballot ruling ‘big loss for Republicans’| | | | | | This decision wasn't the end of this case or the threats against mail-in voting. This case will still need to be decided on the merits ahead of the 2028 elections, and other facets of vote-by-mail, like when a ballot is postmarked, are still under threat. = | | | | = Team: The Supreme Court dropped another "shadow docket" ruling last night, finally blockingTrump and the USPS from implementing his anti-mail-in voting Executive Order. For the midterms, at least. Again, if this is new for you: The "shadow docket." It's the Supreme Court's way to review cases quickly without formal hearings. It's a construct of the last few decades, not widely used before then, but tons of unsigned, pro-Trump rulings have been issued from the Supreme Court this way the last few years. This was another ruling offered on procedural grounds and not the merits of the law. The 7-2 decision will stop the Department of Homeland Security and the Postal Service from creating a national voter registration list and usurping the constitutional authority of the states to run our elections. Even after Justice Kavanaugh signaled that he would have ruled in favor of Trump on the merits of the case, just that it was too close to the midterms for him to support the case right now, a 6-3 win is still worth celebrating in the current political environment, where opponents of voting rights control the White House, Congress, and the Supreme Court. This fight isn't over. The vote suppressors will take every inch they can in their battle to limit voting and invalidate your ballot. The harder they make it to vote, the more cynical, partisan politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. = | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | Experts and our compatriots in the pro-democracy movement were uncertain how the Supreme Court would handle this case. The Court’s past support of even the most legally dubious of Trump’s policies cast into doubt whether the justices would stand against his efforts here , especially after the Court rejected an earlier iteration of this challenge, just weeks ago , on the grounds that it was premature. “ The Supreme Court has made law totally unpredictable ,” election-law expert Justin Levitt told The Atlantic recently, while everyone waited for the Supreme Court to rule. He said “i n a normal world, there would be a zero percent chance ” that the Court would allow the USPS rule to go into effect. Yet, he went on, “ we don’t live in a normal world anymore.” For the time being, let’s celebrate that a semi-rational center of the court held, even as dangers remain ahead in both 2026 and 2028.Let's not forget, while we waited for the Supreme Court to rule, USPS rejected Leon County, Florida’s ballot design because its required printed notation about return mail was 0.014 of an inch too close to other information on the envelope. Trump, MAGA, and the vote suppressors aren't going to stop. He takes these legal decisions on the chin, then comes back with another Executive Order a short time later. He's going to work hard to mess with everyone's votes through this November and beyond. = | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. clean_body: This is a longer email, but I’d appreciate it if you took two minutes to read it | Peter, My name is Joe Males, and I’m running for United States Congress in California’s 25th district. WHO AM I? Like I said, I’m Joe Males. I’m a Mexican-American who was adopted by two wonderful parents when I was four years old. At a young age, I joined the United States Marine Corps to defend our country and ultimately earned the rank of Sergeant before my discharge. Once I entered civilian life, I started my entrepreneurial career owning a successful small computer business until my son took over the family business. Since the Democrats will want to use this to attack me, I will tell you: I was a former Democrat. I switched over to the Republican Party during the Reagan era once I saw what the Democrats truly stood for. I’ve seen firsthand how today’s Democratic Party has abandoned working families. Every single day, I hear from constituents who are struggling with everyday challenges. I hear them, and I fully agree with them. It’s time for change in California. WHY DID I ENTER POLITICS? In short, my son, Nicholas, was tragically stabbed to death and murdered in 2016. If you’re a parent, I’m sure you could imagine how devastating this was for me. Nicholas was only 28 at the time and did not deserve what happened. He had followed in my footsteps and joined the Marine Corps. He was a father to two children – my grandchildren. When it happened, no one came forward with any information, and the case to find the killer went cold. I decided to take a stand, to fight for the rule of law and public safety so that no other family has to experience the same tragedy. Five years later, I ran for City Council in Hemet. I won, and just a few months later, our amazing law enforcement found the killer and arrested him. WHAT ARE MY PRIORITIES AS YOUR NEXT CONGRESSMAN? As a former Democrat turned Republican, I know what the Democrat Party is supposed to represent. But ever since the Reagan era, they’ve continued to move farther and farther to the extreme left. Now, they stand for DEI, wokeness, putting Americans last, and doing everything they can to fight against President Trump. As a Hispanic American who lives in a border district and who was adopted by American parents, I fully believe in LEGAL immigration. America is THE BEST COUNTRY IN THE WORLD! Millions of people around the world want to move here for the American Dream, for the opportunity of a better life, but they must do it THE RIGHT WAY. Our Southern Border has been porous under Joe Biden’s Administration. Living in a border district, I’ve seen firsthand millions of illegal immigrants entering the country with the help of the dangerous Mexican Cartel, many through my hometown, bringing dangerous drugs like fentanyl, trafficking women and children, and committing heinous crimes on our side of the border. This needs to END, and I’m grateful for President Trump’s leadership on this. In Congress, I’ll always defend strong border security. On top of that, I am a firm believer in the America-First Movement. After four years under Joe Biden’s leadership, America has become weak in every aspect. I already mentioned our border security, but our military, social life, and economy have all become weakened under the rule of DEI and wokeness. As a military veteran, it pained me to see the way Joe Biden withdrew from Afghanistan, giving the Taliban millions of dollars worth of high-level American military equipment, which they parade around. Our weakened military presence allowed Russia to invade Ukraine and Hamas to launch terrorist attacks on Israel. I’ll do everything in my power as a Congressman to support our military so we prioritize READINESS over WOKENESS. Finally, we must dismantle DEI in every corner of the government. DOGE’s work to cut wasteful spending has been a great start, but we must continue to fight to lower the cost of living, defend free speech, and usher in the Golden Age of America. WHY DO I NEED YOUR HELP? Simply put – the Radical Left has a stranglehold on California. Just like they’re trying to flip Texas Blue, I’m trying to flip California Red. It may seem impossible, but so many Californians are sick and tired of suffering under Gavin Newsom, Nancy Pelosi, and Adam Schiff’s leadership here. I know many people who have left California just because of the politicians who want to turn our beautiful state into a Communist Utopia. But Newsom, Pelosi, and Schiff have MILLIONS of dollars in reserve, ready to spend against my campaign to prevent common sense leadership. They only care about lining their own pockets, even if their constituents suffer. It’s going to be an uphill battle, but if there’s one thing I learned as a Marine, it’s that the only way to create a better tomorrow is through dedicated hard work and grit. Together, we can fight and WIN. | Thank you for taking the time to read all of this. I truly appreciate it. body:
| Inside Elections was the last major forecaster holding out on our race, and they just shifted their prediction of the Alaska Senate race in our direction. [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/131319?t=6&akid=28890%2E878179%2ERm6Dj-) They’re joining every other major election forecaster in recognizing that the momentum is on our side. They know what we know: **We are going to win this race.**

Alaskans are ready for change. I’ve spent the past nine months traveling to communities in every corner of the state – from Prince of Wales to St. Lawrence Island, the Kenai to the Arctic. And everywhere I go, I hear the same thing: _Enough._

Enough of Dan Sullivan’s self-dealing. He’s _tripled_ his personal wealth since getting to DC, and Alaskans are paying the price. We are getting crushed by corporate greed while he turns the other way, and we’re tired of it.

I’m angry that the millionaires and billionaires have rigged the system in DC against working Alaskans. I’m angry that it doesn’t work for us anymore. But I’m also optimistic. Alaskans are can-do people. And together, on November 3rd, we’re going to take the first step toward taking back our state.

We won nearly 50% of the vote in our open primary election last month, against 15 other candidates of all parties – including incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan.

More than 82,000 Alaskans cast their ballots in favor of our fish, family, freedom campaign for a more abundant Alaska. We beat the incumbent by more than 8 points, and in the first poll of the general election, we’re leading Dan Sullivan by _1 point_ in the final round of ranked choice voting.

Because while Alaskans are sending a clear message that we’re done with the self-dealing politics of the past, we’re going up against the entire DC establishment and their billionaire-backed super PACs – and they are pummeling us with attack ads. They’re noticing the momentum that we’re building in Alaska, and they’re spending BIG to stop us.

That’s why this race is so close. It’s the closest race in the country, a true 50/50 toss-up! And while I feel confident that, in the end, we are going to win, it isn’t going to be an easy fight. We are up against a corrupt DC system, and they’re fighting with everything they have to keep it that way.

[With that in mind, please split a donation between the Voter Protection Project and my campaign for U.S. Senate today.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/131319?t=7&akid=28890%2E878179%2ERm6Dj-) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Mary Peltola and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $7 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/131320?t=8&akid=28890%2E878179%2ERm6Dj-)

I’m proud to be running a grassroots campaign. But it means that each and every one of us has to chip in what we can, when we can, to help us win this all-important race. For Alaska, and for the whole country.

Thank you for your support. It makes all the difference.

\- Mary

name: Dan Schwartz
subject: Governor Moore said I could count on you
body:
Here’s why I’m running in Maryland’s First District:
Hey Peter,
Governor Wes Moore was kind enough to let me introduce myself to you directly, so I'll get right to it.
I'm Dan Schwartz. I'm a dad, a consumer watchdog, and I'm running against MAGA Republican Andy Harris in Maryland's First District. Before this, I spent my career going after banks and corporations when they screwed over working families. Now I'm asking for the chance to do that job in Congress.
Here's where our race stands:
**Dan Schwartz 45%
Andy Harris 44%**
That's a poll in a district Andy Harris has held for fifteen years, and it shows that if we can get the resources we need to communicate with voters, we can win. **[Will you split a donation now between our campaign and Gov. Moore’s to help us do exactly that?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260917-3.HUqUpZ&refcode=em-20260917-3&t=1&akid=1943%2E1086043%2E-_Ns8f)**

body:

| SETTING THE RECORD STRAIGHT:
**AMANDA JANOO QUESTIONS WHETHER DEMOCRATS HAVE RUN THE LEGISLATURE**
**When you’re talking about the affordability crisis in Vermont, the history of the last quarter-century matters a lot! **

Since taking office in 2017, Governor Scott and the Progressive-Democrat majority in the Legislature have repeatedly disagreed on the fundamentals of taxes and spending, education and property taxes, energy costs, healthcare choices, and other major policies affecting affordability in Vermont.

_In fact, from 2018-2024, the Progressive-Democrat majority held veto-proof majorities: meaning they could ignore the minority and the Governor -- and that’s exactly what they did. And Vermonters paid a high price for their out-of-the-mainstream ideas. _

Then the balance changed in 2024. Because Vermonters had enough of the unaffordable policies of the past. Now, in 2026 Amanda Janoo is leading the campaign to blame their failed, unaffordable policies on Governor Scott...

**_They’re even willing to try to rewrite history to do it._**

During an interview with WDEV on Thursday, Amanda Janoo was asked how, as a Democrat-Progressive, she would maintain independence from the legislative majority and respond to concerns about rising taxes.

**Here’s what the interviewer asked Janoo:**

_“So, I'm wondering, as a Democrat-Progressive, how do you not rubber stamp, sort of, what I think you said, you know, 40% tax increases over 5 years under Democrat rule. How do you remain at the top, sort of independent, so that you're not just rubber stamping something that people are resisting right now?” _

Janoo said:

**_“Ummm... well, and it's interesting, because, I mean,__has_ _it been Democrat rule?_**

**_Yes._**

**_Yes, it has._**

Here's the math...

**The Progressive-Democrat alliance has controlled both chambers of Vermont’s Legislature since 2004.** **From the beginning of the 2019 legislative session through the 2024 election, Democrats and Progressives continuously held a veto-proof majority in one chamber of the Vermont Legislature — and during four of those six years, they held veto-proof majorities in _both_.

And they used that power to pass the Clean Heat Standard, the Global Warming Solutions Act, Act 181, a 14% Property Tax Increase in a single year, a 20% increase in DMV fees, $100 million in payroll taxes and more...**

_Governor Scott vetoed each of these bills, and Democrats in the House and Senate overrode him to make certain YOUR costs go up._

In the 2024 election, enough Independents, moderate Democrats, and Republicans were elected to break that supermajority.

**_But, in 2026, they want the power back!_**

We can't let that happen.

There is much more work to do to get Vermont’s fundamentals back into the mainstream and make our state more affordable to live and work.

**_WHY DO WE NEED YOUR HELP?_**

**We need your support to push back against the revisionist history and help to elect commonsense candidates who will finally work the Governor Scott to make Vermont more affordable.**

__Amanda Janoo is right about one thing: It is time for a change... but she is clearly not the person to deliver it.__

**Follow the link to contribute today!**

**Thanks for your support,

Team Scott **

subject: Data centers, affordability, and why Memphis has my heart.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Molder for Congress
body:
This conversation reminded me exactly why I'm running.
This conversation reminded me exactly why I'm running.

| | | | |
---
Hey y’all,
To know Memphis is to love Memphis. I mean that.
I sat down with Eric Barnes and Bill Dries on WKNO's Behind the Headlines to talk about what this city means to me and what I want to fight for when I get to Congress: data centers, affordability, and other issues that are shaping Memphis's future and the futures of families across all 17 counties of this district.
I spent three years in this city during law school. Liz and I lived on Linden Avenue, and I would wake up most mornings with a jog through Midtown. I watched the Tigers break my heart in San Antonio at the Final Four Championship game, but the seed was planted then and there for my love of the University of Memphis and the city of Memphis, too.
Memphis shaped me in ways I am still grateful for. And now I have the chance to fight for it in Washington.

Our campaign huddled to talk through our ad strategy, and I approved a new round of TV ads before we had the funds to pay for it all.

MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo doesn't have to make that kind of bet. When his numbers dip, he picks up the phone and calls a couple of billionaires. Problem solved for him.
I don't have that option. **I have you.**
**[Can you help us close this budget gap by pitching in $5 or any amount today? body:
Eastern Washington has been written off for a long time. Labor is not writing us off.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/pe0xQdmGUKm?e=a7b299e420&c2id=1b040b68f1d062d0c966c24dae99fcb4)
| | I grew up in a union family in Spokane. My father belonged to a union, and what that meant in our house was simple: one job was enough to keep a roof over our heads.
**Today I am proud to share that the Washington State Labor Council, AFL-CIO, has endorsed our campaign in Washington's 5th District.** We need to get this news out to voters right away. [**Will you chip in $5 or $10 to our outreach fund? We hadn’t planned on this good news and this is one of those endorsements that can make a huge difference in a race like this.**](https://us.list-manage.com/ZQQdEhyt1q5?e=a7b299e420&c2id=1b040b68f1d062d0c966c24dae99fcb4)
The WSLC represents more than 650 local unions and 600,000 working people in Washington, from the building trades in Spokane to the packing houses in the Walla Walla Valley to the nurses, teachers, machinists, and plumbers in every town in between.
**This endorsement says as much about who I am as it does about my opponent.**
He supported a trade war that is raising the price of everything we buy and putting our own growers and manufacturers at stake. He’s backed cuts that fall hardest on the rural hospitals and clinics working families here depend on. He has voted lockstep with Speaker Johnson at every opportunity - even when it’s against Eastern Washington.
**This guy has got to go.**
Ballots will be mailed soon and the money we raise this week decides how many voters we tell that our campaign is the one supported by teachers, nurses, laborers, operating engineers, electricians, and thousands more union households across Eastern Washington.
[**Please, chip in today and stand with the 600,000 working people who just stood with us:**](https://us.list-manage.com/11GW3wdYSJz?e=a7b299e420&c2id=1b040b68f1d062d0c966c24dae99fcb4)

body:
Communities are already stopping data centers. Congress can hit the brakes before Big Tech locks us in for decades. | |
---
Peter, **Across the country, communities are standing up to Big Tech’s massive data center buildout, and we are winning**. In fact, just 2 days after Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro received 427 direct messages from our campaign, he signed an executive order announcing significant restrictions on data center projects in what NBC News called a “notable shift” after previously encouraging the industry to build in the state. OnePA members here in Pennsylvania are still organizing for the Governor to support a statewide moratorium on hyperscale data centers under Senate Bill 1359. That fight belongs in Congress too. **Data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity and water while raising utility costs, producing around-the-clock noise, and adding pollution, all while Big Tech demands public subsidies.** In less than 4 years, data centers are projected to consume 12% of all U.S. electricity, roughly as much as all other industries combined. Working families get the bills. Neighborhoods already carrying pollution and disinvestment get treated like sacrifice zones. Big Tech sees our organizing working. So does Donald Trump. He spent this week on Truth Social calling AI data centers “the Greatest Economic Development Engine in History.” His own commenters clapped back, nearly 4 to 1. A New York Times/Siena poll found a majority of likely voters oppose building more of them. In Michigan, Trump-aligned Senate candidate Mike Rogers flipped and backed a pause after The Lever exposed his AI-related investments. **Now, Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have introduced the**** _Artificial Intelligence_ _Data Center Moratorium Act_****to pause new data centers and expansions until protections are in place for our utility bills, our water, our jobs, and our communities.** [**Tell Congress to support the Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez bill and pause the data center boom now.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxhjG7-DrcPdCmyOmMJZYw6jmiWm5sGrmjqK5u8wmap3PzN2RNa4pbwd9YfydoQeEsT2uxZk3bl_5YcZFZ9F04v6iVjQdxQ5CY8EXaiHahvVXDhFieXREoeDGVoWWQoiun-TupO0AHvEG4BliGot2-dAoOs8MN5s8nMMv9_LQBEWBu2aBeHFfWfeBPyRQ0fQ-60hUypxNDOY9G8xeKJMLJQdh879IVWHTPGbwCULxxtdWlbbEFSRlwU4adXCrvv_s1fYWmF8nm1U2UMl4uxpKEJMN9YijPHfwuNz2CTfeneN3znRXyf3XAPaX11uQ2jgwM4KB9v6B3iMlrnb2TUgRaAEg2_KouaE5QMjoudsOvpxOnoT-xRFSBWMg5A2ggyzkHWDqRnwaF7IltGKS95E8yeV5KoG_Oo_ENgkn9QBXTzNA/4u4/OlR6RKR0TQqMFj9K50KXqA/h0/h001.e7WGkewUi7lwGe5ox5YnPb1EHRttJ_6FpEcl1mDXDHk) | | [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxhjG7-DrcPdCmyOmMJZYw6jmiWm5sGrmjqK5u8wmap3PzN2RNa4pbwd9YfydoQeEsT2uxZk3bl_5YcZFZ9F04v6iVjQdxQ5CY8EXaiHahvVXDhFieXREoeDGVoWWQoiun-TupO0AHvEG4BliGot2-dAoOs8MN5s8nMMv9_LQBEWBu2aBeHFfWfeBPyRQ0fQ-6YJ75G6FTVy1IxG-SMC1cKg6BJyBjeUId4KFBFblDOH06XdmuhLrmah05nTNhKywAUC_UdeBOrVC1F8iiEYnWM0L0o5NBc8wMIn4VzjUgr1MVtdL8SoFza8D0oa66uzySYXBtAGbSVMEQV9GCk57af_3sMSWZEHAciz2H71bynfWfiS1LUNvnabNbsR-zIzkbOTYvzpKVTrk00EOToQwgttuQ8Zz_iO0iUyKIRU4NIsQ/4u4/OlR6RKR0TQqMFj9K50KXqA/h1/h001.BvmFttUXPLbC0p-4CvwV9b1CVZuCIU_GWYcmmnePlIY)
